The comments from each letter are listed in the order in which they appear in the individual letter.
(1) Letter number 1.
Comment: A
Response: It is true that the area could have possibly qualified an urban renewal project prior to the flood of 1972. However, this does not run counter to the fact that the recovery of the area will be aided by project activities. For instance, relocation activities will provide an out for some residents who wish to sell their property and leave the threatned area, redevelopment will be designed to cope with future flooding, and in general the project activities will protect not only HUD's investment in the area but also the investment that is being made through S.B.A. loans.
(b) Comment: B.
Response: We agree that the problem does exist. However, project funds are limited and are not available for measure to deal with the problems. It appears to us that completion of the "River Relief Road" would do as much to cure their situations or anything else.
(c) Comment: C.
Response: See corrected page 44.
(d) Comment: D.
Response: It is a well established fact that additional project lighting is a deterrent to crime. We also feel that general up grading of the area will reduce crime. However, we do recognize that this point is arguable.
(e) Comment: E.
Response: See response to Army Corps of Engineers, comment #2 above.
